deckName: KS3 DT · J1 Lesson 6 — Inside the Machine (Teacher Deck)

slides.kicker: OUR LADY'S GRAMMAR SCHOOL · DIGITAL TECHNOLOGY
slides.heading: Inside the Machine
slides.notes:
WHERE THE CLASS IS: coming in, sitting at any PC and logging in.

SAY: welcome them in. Ask them to log in and open the class link.

WHEN TO MOVE: when most pupils are logged in, stop the room. Eyes front.

slides.heading: In this lesson you will…
bullets: Name the seven main parts inside a computer and say what each one does.
Say what the operating system is and what it does.
Say how the processor and memory work together, step after step.
slides.notes:
WHERE THE CLASS IS: eyes front.

SAY: read the three aims slowly.

WHEN TO MOVE: straight on.

slides.heading: What today is about
bullets: A computer is a box of parts. Each part has one job.
Today you open one up, on screen, and fix it.
Then you find out who tells the parts what to do.
You work with a partner. The website picks your partner.
slides.notes:
WHERE THE CLASS IS: eyes front.

SAY: read the four lines. A computer is a box of parts. Each part has one job. Today you open one up, on screen, and fix it.

WHEN TO MOVE: straight on.

slides.heading: Getting started
bullets: Sign in to the class website.
Open Lesson 6.
The website finds your partner. Wait for the screen to say who.
Do not log in on two PCs.
slides.notes:
WHERE THE CLASS IS: at their PCs, about to open Lesson 6.

SAY: read the four lines. The website pairs pupils in the order they arrive. If the class is an odd number, the last three work as a team of three.

WHEN TO MOVE: when every pair has pressed Begin and the patient is on the table. The room now runs itself.

slides.heading: The operation
bullets: Seven parts come out. Each one has a job card.
You and your partner share one patient and take turns.
Read what the patient says on screen. There is no sound.
slides.notes:
WHERE THE CLASS IS: working in pairs on the operating table, for about sixteen minutes.

SAY: nothing, once they are in. Walk round and ask one question: what did the patient just say? Never tell them which card is right.

WHEN TO MOVE: when most pairs are on the contest.

slides.heading: The contest
bullets: Four rounds against your partner.
The same question on both screens.
Nobody sees your answer until you have both answered.
One point for each right answer.
slides.notes:
WHERE THE CLASS IS: each pupil playing against the partner, for about twenty-four minutes.

SAY: read the four lines. A pupil who answers fast waits for the partner. Encourage the slower one, not the fast one.

WHEN TO MOVE: about minute 45, or when most pairs are on the extra jobs. Pupils who finish the contest do the extra jobs until you call STOP.

slides.heading: STOP · Exit check
bullets: Four questions, on your own.
Then How did it go?
slides.notes:
WHERE THE CLASS IS: on the extra jobs, or finishing the contest. Stop the room. Eyes front for one minute.

SAY: STOP. Click Finish the lesson. These four questions are on your own. They are marked, and you see every answer on your Live tab. A pair still in the contest finishes it first. Their next screen shows Finish the lesson.

WHEN TO MOVE: send them in. As they finish How did it go?, put the last slide up.

slides.heading: Before you leave
bullets: Sign out.
Leave the PC as you found it.
slides.notes:
WHERE THE CLASS IS: finishing How did it go?

SAY: end on what they achieved. Today you took a computer apart and put it right. See you in a fortnight.

WHEN TO MOVE: before anyone leaves, check that every pupil has finished How did it go? and signed out.
